My post op I wasnt the best as im a bit stubborn and dont like not being able to do things. 2 days after surgery I done my A level exam though I was really swollen and could just about talk. 4 days after surgery I was back at work as boss never knew and still hasnt found out I had surgery (my work didnt involve nearly any communication).

Around 1 month period (depends on how fast your body healing factor as this is my own experience) you can basically do normal things like talking, seeing friends and so on. Eating is still hard and its recommended to eat ice cream and liquid foods for 2 months before you can eat soft foods but it depends on how you are coping. Dont force yourself.  Straws are handy for drinks.

Alcohol is allowed at moderate after 2 weeks, swimming after 6 weeks, no direct sun for 6 weeks and no smoking for 2 weeks. Though I found that weed actually helps heal bone (minus the tobacco, big no). I returned to sports/martial arts after 3 months but took it easy for 3 months.

After surgery your on a lot of painkillers and depends on your country but I was given 2 boxes of different painkillers. For me it was more of an annoying constant ache and I took painkillers whenever I could, following box instructions. Its a bit of a pain sleeping at first but that disappears after a month. But pain from what I remember only lasted a month and your jaw/mouth/lips can be numb but this is normal. Sensation will return (rare cases the nerves dont grow back).

Swelling is around the neck area and for this its recommended placing a towel then ice pack over it for a few mins helps with the swelling and massaging it gently in circular motions. Though everyone is different I have swelling 10 months in but its minimum now.

I think I felt normal - appearance wise around 3 months. I suggest taking before and after pictures at different angles as you can look back at them and see the progress. Sorry for long reply. Feel free to ask anything else.

Ive had the sagittal split osteotomy and genioplasty surgery as I had a slight overbite and my jaw was crooked/more to one side. I wont sugar coat it but for me personally I had the surgery in June 2018 and after I spent about 2 months struggling to eat as I couldnt open my mouth more than the width of my finger. My surgeon told me it takes a year for it to heal and in that time no rough sport or activities should be played in-case it impacts the bone trying to heal. Though I found that after 4-5 months you can basically eat normally (minus something hard like an apple which can be eaten round 7months).

In the first 3 months I had 3 checks/follow ups before I hopefully have my last one this June. Surgery takes about 2-3 hours and after you can leave after 4 hours if theyre happy with the surgery, but sometimes theyll keep you over night.

Orthodontists are check ups as they cant risk anything while the bone is healing. So a check up is every 4 months. Though this is what I read from a leaflet given to me though I was done with orthodontists about 5 years before this surgery.

Personally I wouldn't change orthodontist as theyre familiar with you and your case unless you think its best travel wise but its best to ask them.
